meta.move: Long messages with curly quotes and a concession
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it. Why does my son have a zero?

I want to be fair to Owen. I compared the essay with his in-class writing from September 24: 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices throughout, no quotations. This essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and none of those errors.
I'm writing down September 24, 380 words, forty minutes. A timed in-class paragraph and a weekend essay are two different things, Hale. Did you put any of this to Owen before the zero went in?
You’re right that the checker alone proves nothing. I’m taking it off the table. I’m relying on the writing and the version history.
Okay. You still haven't told me whether Owen was heard before the zero. And "version history" isn't a document, Hale. What does it say?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. The zero must come off Owen's essay, and I still need to know whether he was heard before it was entered. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn and a straight answer on whether Owen was heard first.
What moved her: Hale dropped the detector score and set a dated in-class sample against the essay, which gave her one small sign of ground because it was specific and something she could check.
What cost ground: Hale never answered her question about whether Owen was heard before the zero, and named the version history without giving any times or content, so she had nothing to read.
Try next time: When she asks whether Owen was heard first, answer that directly in one sentence, then put the version history in front of her with its times.
